claims.head: The matchup inside the matchup
claims.body: The Flames are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Hurricanes are the best at keeping shots away. Hot take: the Hurricanes shut it down.
claims.call: The Hurricanes keep the Flames’ shot volume score under 100, the league average.

claims.head: Bahl and Nemec get the Aho assignment
claims.call: The Flames’ P1 (Bahl and Nemec) spends at least 43% of its 5-on-5 time against the Hurricanes’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Flames keep sending Bahl and Nemec out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Huska has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Hurricanes’ first line is Carrier, Aho and Svechnikov.

claims.gist: At home, Ryan Huska likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Hurricanes’ first line.

notes.text: Seth Jarvis is out and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward. William Carrier has taken his spot beside Sebastian Aho and Andrei Svechnikov.
Taylor Hall is out (upper-body injury) and missed their last game.
Jordan Staal is out 1-2 months (calf tear) and has missed the last 2 games. Mark Jankowski has taken his spot beside Jordan Martinook and Nikolaj Ehlers.
Alexander Nikishin has not played this season. He is a top-four defenseman. Mike Reilly has taken his spot beside Shayne Gostisbehere.
Logan Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 8 games, up from 1% last season.

faceoff.text: Jordan Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 46% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 20 seconds at a time, against 64 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Nikolaj Ehlers (17 of 20 changes).

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 7 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 45%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Samuel Honzek is out week to week (lower body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Yegor Sharangovich has taken his spot beside Mikael Backlund and Joel Farabee.
Joel Hanley has not dressed for the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Jake Middleton has taken his spot beside Zayne Parekh.
Jonathan Huberdeau is on injured reserve (hip surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, up from 2% last season.

CGY.head: The Hurricanes should be favored
CGY.body: Even though Calgary has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. To pull this off, the Flames can start with getting good looks, plus a goalie who steals the show.

CAR.head: The Hurricanes should be in control
CAR.body: Even though Calgary has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. If the Flames want to spoil it, start with getting good looks.

story.head: The Hurricanes are rolling
paras: The Flames are 1-6-0. The Hurricanes are on a tear, six straight wins.

It’s strength against strength: the Flames are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Hurricanes are the best at keeping shots away. At home, Ryan Huska likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Canes’ first line.

items.text: The Hurricanes are newly without Taylor Hall and Jordan Staal, and have had to make do without Seth Jarvis and Alexander Nikishin all season.
The Flames are newly without Samuel Honzek, have been without Joel Hanley since Oct 3, and have had to make do without Jonathan Huberdeau all season.
Mark Jankowski has scored in five straight games.
Sebastian Aho has a point in seven straight games.
